title: 2025 budget confirmed with 6.34% tax increase
subtitle: Utility rates, fee increases, four-unit four-storey zoning, reserve policy changes and a military squadron anniversary
overview: Council reaffirmed the 2025 operating budget, which carries a combined property tax increase of 6.34% and a tax levy of $107,321,892. Staff also proposed a net-zero set of adjustments to cover new cost pressures without changing the rate. These include higher revenue estimates, a 5% capital overhead charge and a one-year cut to contributions to three capital and climate reserve funds {{vote:m11}}.

Council approved 2025 City Utilities rates. The water rate is $2.48/m3 and the sanitary rate is $2.93/m3, with new stormwater rates by property type {{vote:m10}}. Staff said the average household impact is a 6.4% increase. Council also raised building standards fees by 12% {{vote:m4}}, rental housing fees by 4.5% and business licensing fees by 5% {{vote:m2}}.

Council approved the city-wide zoning change allowing up to four units in four storeys on low-rise residential lots {{vote:m12}}. Delegates mostly supported it, while some raised parking, drainage and lot coverage concerns. Council also updated its financial policy thresholds and reserve rules, and received the asset management report cards.

decisions.detail: Council reaffirmed the 2025 operating budget with a combined 6.34% tax increase, approved net-zero adjustments, added two externally funded positions and restarted the Development Charge by-law update.
Council approved the city-initiated zoning amendment permitting up to four units and four storeys as of right in low-rise residential areas.
Council set 2025 water, sanitary and stormwater rates and approved the 2026-2034 rate forecast in principle.
Council approved a 12% increase to all Building Standards fees and charges effective January 1, 2025.

decisions.item: Rental housing and business licensing fees
decisions.detail: Council approved a 4.5% rental housing rate increase and a 5% business licensing increase for 2025, with 2026 forecasts approved in principle.
Council approved updated financial request policy FC-002, folded the credit balances policy into it, and approved the updated investment policy.
Council set how surplus Enova dividend income is split among three reserve funds and approved revised reserve policies.
Council approved 2025 cemetery fees, allowed the Cemetery Reserve Fund to run a deficit at times until the end of 2033, and directed staff to propose a funding solution.

debate: On the budget, one councillor said they were not seeking to reopen it but was concerned about trimming contributions to the climate and infrastructure reserve funds. Staff said removing those two reductions would add a small tax increase, about $5 for the average household. Staff said the reductions were set so reserves stay at approved levels and no capital projects are affected.

On revenue assumptions, a councillor asked whether the assessment growth, recreation revenue and investment income increases were sustainable. Staff said they were, with cautious estimates, while noting that falling interest rates will reduce investment income over time.

On the zoning change, councillors asked about parking, stormwater, shadow impacts, tree canopy and accessibility. Staff said changes are expected to be gradual and can be monitored. Lot-level stormwater is addressed at the building permit stage, and the lot coverage limit follows provincial rules. Staff said they would follow up on accessibility under the building code.

Delegates and residents largely supported four units in four storeys. A housing developer said the fourth storey makes accessible, family-sized units feasible. One delegate urged eliminating parking minimums entirely, while a resident said the minimums should stay for now and asked for a minimum landscaped area to limit flooding.
On the financial policy update, the mayor suggested a regular review timeline for approval thresholds that had not changed in about 17 years. Staff agreed to explore it.
